articleTitle: Evaluation of a Dual Axial Ankle Supporter with Adjustable Assisting Direction Mechanism for Plantarflexion and Dorsiflexion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Mountaineering accidents frequently lead to lower limb injuries, particularly affecting the ankles. Ankle twisting is a common injury occurring during downhill descents. In particular, walking on cross-slopes can result in abnormal inversion or eversion of the ankle, increasing the risk of injuries. While numerous ankle assistive devices exist for walking conventional ones are often unsuitable for navigating uneven terrain. To address the challenges of cross-slope walking, we developed a dual axial ankle supporter (DAAS), featuring dual axial movement in both the sagittal and frontal planes. Its structure includes a cuff, elastic connector, main frame, adjustable assisting direction mechanism (AADM), and fixed parts. Each foot’s DAAS weighs approximately 285 g. Gait experiments were conducted to assess the assistive effects of the DAAS. In evaluating the impact of the elastic connector, EMG signals from the peroneus longus is measured during cross-slope walking. The findings indicate that the elastic connector of the DAAS successfully reduced muscle activations of the peroneus longus on the uphill of the cross-slope.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Permeability of Thermoresponsive Microgel Valves for Single-Cell Analysis Devices*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: In recent years, microfluidic devices have attracted large attention as a tool for single-cell analysis. Among the components of microfluidic devices, valves are important for fluid control in devices. Our group have proposed on-chip microvalves made of a thermoresponsive hydrogel that can be actuated by using light irradiation. By using the light irradiation for actuation, we can integrate a large number of microvalves and drive them independently without complex wirings. This integrated microvalve can be used for single cell manipulations for analyses, such as trap, transport, mechanical stimulation or chemical stimulation. In this study, we evaluate permeability of some chemical reagents to the hydrogel valves to confirm possibility of application of the valves for chemical stimuli. We varied sizes of microgel valves and molecular weight of chemicals and evaluate permeation time for the design of gel valves that are suitable for single-cell analysis.

articleTitle: Development and Application of an Exercise-promoting System for the Elderly with a Gait Indicator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Regular exercise is highly recommended by the World Health Organization to maintain personal health, especially for the elderly. However, it is difficult to maintain motivation through time while going through degradation as one grows older. Additionally, the elderly’s motions might become incorrect as the muscle’s strength is reduced. To encourage the elderly to exercise more, an exercise-promoting system is proposed so that exercising can be more entertaining. The system is built with a gaming concept, in which there are obstacles for the users to avoid and rewards to collect. However, instead of controlling the avatar in the game with a joystick or keyboard, we used a gait indicator, developed by our laboratory, to detect the user’s current walking speed and status. Additionally, haptic speakers are attached to the device so that throughout the game, the device can inform the users to do corresponding actions according to the game environment. In the experiment, users with this system showed a significant increase in focusing in the exercise, compared to normal exercise. Additionally, the system allows the user to consume more calories in a shorter walking distance. With the proposed system, we expect it can make exercising more enjoyable for the elderly and encourage them to exercise more to maintain their health.

articleTitle: Fixation of engineered skeletal muscle fiber using magnetically induced mechanical interlocking for micro mechanical structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Engineering skeletal muscle fibers are expected to be used as bio-actuators because they bring various advantages of biological materials to actuators, such as the ability to operate at much smaller sizes. However, to prevent muscle fibers from malfunctioning due to spontaneous shrinkage during culture, fixation during the culture process is necessary. Furthermore, to prevent muscle fibers from breaking during fixation and considering the load reduction for bio-actuators, this study combines our previously proposed method of creating magnetic ends at both ends of muscle fibers, and uses magnets to attract the magnetic ends to achieve fixation on 3D-printed fixation parts based on mechanical interlocking. By using measurement system consists of electrical slider and strain gauge, tensile test was applied to the muscle fiber fixed on 3D printed fixation part. We found that magnetic ends remained fixation on fixation part even muscle fiber was stretched to break, with a maximum tensile force $600 \mu \mathrm{~N}$.

articleTitle: A hierarchical framework for collision avoidance in robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) procedures benefit significantly from robotic systems due to their improved precision and dexterity. However, ensuring safety in these dynamic and cluttered environments is an ongoing challenge. This paper proposes a novel hierarchical framework for collision avoidance in MIS. This framework integrates multiple tasks, including maintaining the Remote Center of Motion (RCM) constraint, tracking desired tool poses, avoiding collisions, optimizing manipulability, and adhering to joint limits. The proposed approach utilizes Hierarchical Quadratic Programming (HQP) to seamlessly manage these constraints while enabling smooth transitions between task priorities for collision avoidance. Experimental validation through simulated scenarios demonstrates the framework’s robustness and effectiveness in handling diverse scenarios involving static and dynamic obstacles, as well as inter-tool collisions.

articleTitle: RNNPB-based Shared Control for Maintaining Sense of Agency in Robotic Teleoperation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: The sense of agency (SoA), the feeling of recognizing that the observed movement is caused by oneself, which is important in robot teleoperation, is reduced by shared control, in which the robot and the human cooperate to control the robot. In this study, we developed a system that uses a recurrent neural network with parametric biases (RNNPB) trained on expert operational data to predict the next input from nonexperts and convert it into robot commands in real time. Through an experiment with a pouring task, it was confirmed that the proposed method outputs predicted values that spatially and temporally interpolate the operational inputs, gradually correcting the robot’s movements to align with the experts’ trajectories. The proposed method showed a high SoA comparable to direct control; however, no statistically significant difference in task performance was observed. Future work aims to improve the generality of the model to accommodate a wider variety of input trajectories.

articleTitle: Transition of Peri-personal Space by Making Robot Hands Transparent and Displaying Virtual Hands to Improve the Accuracy of Position Grasping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: In recent years, teleoperated robots have been developed to provide work and experience without physically human mobility. When working or experiencing through teleoperation, reaching and grasping an object is a frequent task. However, it is difficult to reach and grasp an object accurately. The main reason is that depth perception is reduced, and it is difficult for the operators to grasp the robot’s surroundings in the same way that they grasp their own surroundings on a daily basis. Therefore, an interface is proposed in which the teleoperated robot hands are made transparent from the images sent from the teleoperated follower side, and virtual hands are displayed at the position and posture where the robot hands existed. The virtual hands display enhances the embodiment of the robot hands and transfers the peri-personal space (PPS) around the person to the robot hands, which enables accurate recognition of the location of objects. Experiments of reaching and grasping showed that displaying the virtual hands reduced the time to complete the task by 19.9 percent and significantly improved the success rate of grasping, compared to viewing the robot hands. In addition, it was confirmed that the virtual hands were more embodied when the virtual hands were displayed. Thus, this interface was confirmed to transfer the PPS around the robot hands and improve the accuracy of position grasping.

articleTitle: An adaptive filter for surface EMG measurement during FES
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Biopotential signals have been used as command and feedback signals in systems using functional electrical stimulation (FES) of motor nerves to restore the lost function. To use the voluntary electromyography (EMG) as a control signal for the FES of the same muscle, it is necessary to suppress the M-wave evoked by the electrical stimulation. The methods used in previous studies are prone to excessive elimination of signals or residual artifacts. When the experimental environment changes, changes in many parameters will lead to inconvenience in application. In view of the shortcomings of the existing technology, this paper proposes an adaptive filter for surface EMG measurement during electrical stimulation. The filter filtering out electrical stimulation artifacts from surface EMG signals using templates that can adapt to different experimental individuals and changes in electrode positions. There are no special requirements for the degree of aliasing of muscle electrical signals. It enables online filtering synchronized with electrical stimulation and can be used in real-time systems. The experimental results on 7 healthy subjects suggested that the filter can effectively filter out electrical stimulation artifacts without deteriorating EMG.

articleTitle: Contactless Bioprinting Based on Acoustic Tweezer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: 3D bioprinting technology presents an expansive array of possibilities for tissue engineering, drug screening, and foundational research. However, its operational demands necessitate a meticulous balance between pollution prevention and minimizing cellular harm. Traditional inkjet and extrusion bioprinting methods lead to direct nozzle-to-object contact, heightening the risk of contamination and cellular injury. To address these challenges, we propose a novel bioprinting approach harnessing acoustic tweezer in conjunction with a three-degree-of-freedom displacement platform. Herein, hydrogel droplets containing cells are trapped by acoustic tweezer and subsequently transported and positioned at the desired location via the displacement platform. This innovative technique avoids direct nozzle contact with the printed object, thus offering a viable strategy for mitigating contamination and minimizing cellular damage throughout the printing process.

articleTitle: Wearable Fabric Actuator Inducing Shoulder Movements for Directional Guidance of Hand Movements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: In recent years, there has been an increasing focus on teleoperation of robots via immersive environments. These systems require haptic sensation to the hand for intuitive teleoperation. However, most methods for providing haptic sensation to the hand may interfere with hand position acquisition by vision and other devices. Thus, there is a need for a method that can coexist with the acquisition of hand information. This paper presents a method for guiding directions of hand movements in immersive environments using McKibben-based haptic sensations, which can coexist with the acquisition of hand information. The proposed system employs a wearable fabric actuator consisting of four McKibben-type artificial muscles that induce internal rotation, external rotation, internal abduction, and external abduction of the shoulder. By combining these four haptic sensations, the proposed system can guide the direction of hand movements without interfering with hand information acquisition by other devices. An algorithm is implemented to effectively combine the four haptic sensations based on the target guiding direction. We evaluated the accuracy and speed of the proposed system through a participant experiment.

articleTitle: Improvement of the Biomolecular Artificial Muscle in Mechanical Properties and Three-dimensional Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Molecular motors are a promising research direction, offering advantages such as self-organization, scalability, and energy transfer efficiency, which significantly promote advancements in the field of microrobots. This research aims to enhance the properties of biomolecular artificial muscles and address the inherent limitations they face. Firstly, the improvement is focused on the contraction motion of the biomolecular artificial muscles. We hypothesize that microtubules play a crucial role in the function of biomolecular artificial muscles and expect that external force fields, such as fluid flow fields, can influence and control the alignment of microtubules, thereby enhancing force generation. Preliminary results have shown that the mean velocity and orientation of microtubules can indeed be affected and controlled by the fluid flow field which basically proved the possibility of the assumption. Additionally, exploring the application of biomolecular artificial muscle is also a vital task for us. Currently, biomolecular artificial muscles have been validated but also restricted for planar contraction motion, which limits the further utilizations of micromanipulation. To achieve motility not only on the x-y axis but also in the z direction, a specific experimental setup has been demonstrated that the micro gripper prototyped and integrated with the microstructures is designed and proposed for this purpose. The biomolecular artificial muscle would be chosen as the activated source of the microgripper and predicted to achieve the aspiration of three-dimensional micromanipulation.

articleTitle: S-CycleGAN: Semantic Segmentation Enhanced CT-Ultrasound Image-to-Image Translation for Robotic Ultrasonography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Ultrasound imaging is pivotal in various medical diagnoses due to its non-invasive nature and safety. In clinical practice, the accuracy and precision of ultrasound image analysis are critical. Recent advancements in deep learning are showing great capacity of processing medical images. However, the data hungry nature of deep learning and the shortage of high-quality ultrasound image training data suppress the development of deep learning based ultrasound analysis methods. To address these challenges, we introduce an advanced deep learning model, dubbed S-CycleGAN, which generates high-quality synthetic ultrasound images from computed tomography (CT) data. This model incorporates semantic discriminators within a CycleGAN framework to ensure that critical anatomical details are preserved during the style transfer process. The synthetic images are utilized to enhance various aspects of our development of the robot-assisted ultrasound scanning system. The data and code will be available at https://github.com/yhsong98/ct-us-i2i-translation.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of Biomimetic Assist Suits *
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: In sagittal plane, movements of knee joints are relative motions between femur and tibia, which is a combination of sliding and rolling motion. The motion causes misalignment between the biological axis and the mechanical axis of the orthosis. We developed the semi-active knee joint (SKJ) with an adjustable reaction force mechanism, which can adjust the force applied depending on the flexion angle. The SKJ uses femur and tibia gears to mimic the motion of the knee joint. However, the existing SKJ comprises two linear motion springs arranged in series, making the mechanism larger in the vertical direction. To solve this problem, this paper reports the design and development of the SKJ type-P, achieving a reduced size and improved operability. We also report the development of a biomimetic assist suit (BAS) combined with knee and ankle aids, and the experiments performed to verify its effectiveness. The gait results obtained from the experiment did not confirm a significant decrease in muscle activity when wearing the BAS, except in a few cases. The reasons for this are that the assistive torque of SKJ is insufficient when the knee flexion angle is at its maximum during walking. On the other hand, attaching the BAS did not cause any increase in burden, which indicates the success of the proposed lightweight design.

articleTitle: Thermoelectrically Induced Thermal Stimuli in Madagascar Hissing Cockroach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Electrical stimulation of the antennae and cerci is a common method for controlling cockroach movement, but it presents limitations such as invasiveness and habituation. This research explores alternative method for manipulating cockroach locomotion. One promising approach is thermal stimulation, which leverages the insect’s natural sensitivity to temperature changes. Our study aims to utilize thermal stimulation to trigger an aversion response in cockroaches, thereby influencing their behavior. The experimental setup involved recording cockroach movements with a high-resolution camera and analyzing their escape responses under various thermal stimuli conditions. Our findings demonstrate that heat stimulation can trigger cockroach movement, inducing both forward motion and turning behaviors.

articleTitle: Advancing Biohybrid Insect Robot (BIR) Locomotion Control Through Non-Invasive Mechanical Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Insects exhibit remarkable sensory capabilities, including keen vision, sensitive olfaction, and tactile receptors, enabling them to navigate and interact with their surroundings proficiently. Leveraging these sensory organs, biohybrid insect robots (BIRs) have emerged as a significant research interest over the past decade for a wide array of applications. However, the prevailing methodology for BIR development predominantly involves invasive techniques and electrical pulses to control locomotion, posing potential risks to the insect’s sensory organs. In response, this study introduces a non-invasive mechanical stimulation approach to govern BIR locomotion, reducing the likelihood of impairing the insect’s sensory organs. Two piezo actuators are applied to both antennae, and a vibration motor is attached to the back of the cockroach near the cerci. Based on experimental results, we successfully demonstrated locomotion control for both forward and stop movements. A square wave signal with a frequency of 300 Hz was selected as the piezo actuator’s input signal to stop the BIR’s movement. The proposed mechanical stimulation achieves a noteworthy $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ average accuracy in controlling BIR forward and stop movements, marking a significant advancement in developing non-invasive control for biohybrid insect robots.

articleTitle: Myriapod robot locomotion control using central pattern generator based on Kuramoto oscillator model*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Online trajectory generation for myriapod robots with multiple degrees of freedom with neural control is still a difficult and unsolved problem. For this, we have designed a control architecture based on central pattern generators (CPGs) implemented as a system of coupled nonlinear oscillators of Kuramoto type. The CPG, like its biological counterpart, can produce coordinated patterns of rhythmic activity. To test our controller, we designed a simple myriapod robot with twelve actuated legs capable of walking on ground. A ring of 12 oscillators with projection of phase using a piecewise linear function serves as the CPG controller. Such a network running on specialized Tweensy 4.0 micro controller board takes around 24 kilo bytes of memory (only 0.2% of micro controller dynamic access memory capacity) to execute walking mode of locomotion. Results are presented demonstrating the basic locomotion pattern such as forward, right turning, and left turning movement of the robot and robustness of forward movement with respect to neural disruption of muted oscillators.

articleTitle: Contact Detection of Forceps for a Vitreoretinal Surgical Simulator Using Infrared Reflection Images of Forceps
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: To train for vitreoretinal surgeries, such as peeling of the inner limiting membrane, a surgical simulator with an elaborate retinal model and method of contact detection is necessary. Quantitative evaluation of forceps contacts to the retinal model is required because excessive forceps contact can cause loss of eyesight. This paper presents a detection method using image analysis to detect forceps contact with the retinal model. An evaluation system for contact detection of forceps was constructed, which includes an optical system incorporating an 850 nm LED, a CCD camera, and an infrared pass filter placed under a retinal model. This system observes the reflected light of infrared light at the forceps tips and evaluates the variation of the forceps shape. The luminance value of the forceps tips edge was set as a common threshold used for each frame and the number of pixels with luminance higher than the threshold was counted before and after forceps contact. As a result of image analysis, we confirmed that the number of counted pixels increased immediately after forceps contact and by evaluating the change in the number of counted pixels, we succeeded in detecting forceps contact at a load of less than 0.1 mN within a radius of $2 \mu \mathrm{~m}$.

articleTitle: RCM Constrained Task Space Trajectory Generation for Autonomous Robotic Surgeries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: As the field of Surgical Robotics progresses towards achieving autonomy, there has been a noticeable increase in the utilization of generic serial manipulators for these applications. For Minimally Invasive Surgeries, it is required to impose a motion constraint with respect to the incision point on the patient. This brings up a complexity in their motion control complying to the constraint. With the requirements of having the least violation of this Remote Centre of Motion (RCM) constraint and accuracy of the end-effector, several control strategies have been put forth and evaluated using different manipulators. However, trajectory generation in the surgical environment remains a challenge to be addressed for autonomous robotic surgeries that are minimally invasive. In this paper, we propose an RCM constrained task space trajectory generation algorithm for autonomous MIS applications. The algorithm, independent of the manipulator kinematics, utilizes unevenly distributed visual point cloud data in task space for path generation and follows a uniform displacement per unit time step approach for trajectory generation and tracking. The proposed algorithm is implemented on a KUKA LBR iiwa robot using simulated visual data that effectively illustrates the surgical scenario. The key validation metrics, RCM violation error and tool-tip tracking error are well within the acceptable range for the test case implemented.

articleTitle: Target Motion Estimation by Multi-Eye Vision Hand-Arm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a “Multi-Eye Vision Hand-Arm,” in which many small high-speed cameras are mounted on the entire body of a hand-arm robot to eliminate blind spots in visual recognition. Also, we propose a method to estimate the trajectory of a moving object by integrating asynchronous visual information from each high-speed camera with a nonlinear Kalman filter. We realized ball tracking and catching to confirm the system’s effectiveness.

articleTitle: Towards Mathematical Modeling of Tissue-Engineered Skeletal Muscle Considering Contraction-Induced Stiffness Changes*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Recently, bio-hybrid devices using muscle tissue or muscle cells as a drive source have been actively studied. Although there have been many reports on the development of bioactuators, most of them are concerned with muscle tissue culture and assembly methods, and very few studies have been conducted from the control engineering perspective of tissue-engineered muscle actuators. It is known that the stiffness of muscle changes between relaxation and excitation, and in particular, empirically, tissue-engineered muscle is immature compared to biological muscle, so the change in stiffness during contraction is relatively very large. Therefore, we will first evaluate the change in stiffness of cultured muscle during relaxation and contraction by a push test and confirm that the stiffness increases significantly with TESM. In addition, it is difficult to represent this large change in stiffness using the conventional Hill’s four-element model. Therefore, this study proposes a model of TESM in which two active elements that are involved only during contraction are added to Hill’s four-element model. The force equations for these isometric tests are derived. As a next step, we plan to experimentally identify the parameters to confirm the validity of this model.

articleTitle: Frog Cyborg That Exhibits Vertical Jumping by Snap-through Buckling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: We intend to develop a frog cyborg that can jump vertically by exploiting the snap-through buckling mechanism of the trunk structure. We focused on the exceptional vertical jumping motion of Rana tagoi. We confirmed that the snap-through buckling mechanism occurred during vertical jumping but not during horizontal jumping. The snap-through buckling mechanism was confirmed biomechanically using a dissected frog. We developed a frog cyborg that is controlled by driving the leg and the trunk joints by electrical stimulations. As a result of experiments, we confirmed that the frog cyborg can jump vertically by simultaneously activating the leg muscles and the trunk muscles.

articleTitle: Simulation of Epileptic Seizure Suppression through Extracellular Potassium Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Epilepsy, a disabling condition impacting millions globally, remains largely refractory to standard pharmacological treatments in about one third of cases. Current alternative strategies include surgical resection of affected tissue or invasive neuromodulatory techniques like deep brain stimulation, though these methods often face significant limitations due to their non-specific and potentially disruptive nature. In this study, we employed network simulations to explore a novel approach based on the modulation of extracellular ion concentrations. Specifically, we investigated how manipulating extracellular potassium concentration could influence the behavior of an excitatory-inhibitory neural network affected by induced, focal epilepsy. Our simulations demonstrate the potential effectiveness of a theoretical device designed to alter potassium ion concentrations in blocking epileptic-like activity at its onset.

articleTitle: Automatic Stiffness Measurement of Small Objects Using an Integrated System of Simultaneous Multi-scale Observation and Two-Directional Force Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Recently, the field of life sciences has witnessed significant advancements, leading to the exploration of various cell characteristics to evaluate cellular behavior. Among these characteristics, cell stiffness has garnered considerable attention. It is widely acknowledged that cell stiffness undergoes changes based on the cell’s physiological state, rendering stiffness measurement a critical parameter in cell evaluation. However, the extensive research into cell stiffness has been hindered by the challenges associated with manipulating micron-scale cells and measuring nano-scale forces. Previous studies have proposed a cell stiffness measurement system utilizing a two-fingered microhand equipped with a micro force sensor. Nonetheless, this approach required manual manipulation of the target object, resulting in potential errors in stiffness measurement. Additionally, manual manipulation restricted the workspace, limiting its applicability. To address these limitations, this paper introduces an automated stiffness measurement technique that integrates force data and image data. Furthermore, a multi-scale simultaneous observation system is presented, combining optical systems from two microscopes with different magnification levels.

articleTitle: Investigation of Sensory Provision for Calf and Shin Using Fabric Actuator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Various haptic devices are attracting attention in many fields, and research and development on haptic devices using soft actuators are underway. We developed a fabric actuator that is flexible and freely deformable soft actuator. This actuator is expected to be used in haptic devices, and it was clarified the device can evoke Grasp, Pinch, Press, and Twist tactile at one actuator in the upper arm and forearm. We focus on the site extensibility of this actuator. In this paper, we verified what types of tactile sensations this actuator can evoke in the shin and calf via experiments with one experimenter as the subject. As a result, mainly three results were obtained: The first was the area where the tactile work was accurately answered. Second, the subject was confused about whether the pattern was Press or Grasp. Third, it was difficult to evoke Pinch tactile. After consideration, it was suggested that the method of attachment is important. In the future, we aim to achieve diverse tactile recall with the leg while investigating other causes.

articleTitle: Fixed-point magnetothermal effect in symmetric double-axis gradient field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Fixed-point magnetothermal effect is a technology that enables precise heating and minimizes the impact on unnecessary heating areas. In this study, we propose a symmetric double-axis gradient magnetic field for magnetic field hyperthermia (MFH) based on this technique. Unlike the previous asymmetric single-axis gradient magnetic field, this new magnetic field allows for a more stable, regular-shaped and contractile free field point (FFP). Magnetothermal experiments conducted at different hole locations demonstrate the effective realization of the fixed-point magnetothermal effect using the symmetric double-axis gradient magnetic field.

articleTitle: Verification of Mehcanism How Fabric Actuator Evoke Pinched Tactile by Using Force Distribution Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Various haptic devices are attracting attention in many fields. However, conventional haptic devices have some limits. Electrical stimulation devices are lightweight and flexible, but the area in which the tactile stimulation is provided is spatially limited, and the variation of the tactile stimulation is few. The mechanical stimulation method can provide a widely stable tactile sensation, but it requires a rigid drive or limited mounting area. We developed a fabric actuator that is flexible and freely deformable soft actuator. This actuator is expected to be used in haptic devices, and it was clarified that the device can evoke an unprecedented pinched sensation by the wearer’s sensation. However, it was not clear what mechanism evoked the pinched tactile. In this paper, we used a distribution sensor that can measure shear force to clarify the mechanism. Based on the results of the experiments, it was clarified that the three-dimensional intersections of the artificial muscles evoke a variety of force directions, contributing to the induction of the pinched tactile stimuli that were not previously possible.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Simple Prosthetic Arm Usage for a Patient with Four-limb Deficiency Walking on Powered Knee Prostheses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Walking is one of the most fundamental and convenient locomotion to move for relatively short distance. Walking behaver is achieved by combination of whole body motions of legs, arms, trunk and other parts of body. Human walks extremely in an efficient way using musculoskeletal system, and, once human loses some part of body, he is often unable to walk normally. Especially, it is quite challenging for a patient with severe disability such as four limb deficiency to walk like a normal human even with cutting-edge prosthetic technologies. In this study, suitable walking behavior for a patient with four limb deficiency is investigated with simple prosthetic arms (PAs) and powered knee prostheses knee with a series elastic actuator (PKP-SEA). As a result, unique walking gait is acquired unlike normal human. Moreover, prosthetic arm usage contributes mainly in sagittal plane to increase his stride.

articleTitle: Placement Optimization for Humanoid Robot Manipulation Using a Task-Driven Planning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Planning a placement is crucial for humanoid robots to successfully execute specific manipulation tasks. While a feasible solution of placement ensures that the end-effector can reach the desired poses, it does not specify the arm configuration during the task. This paper introduces a task-driven planning method to optimize placement for manipulation tasks, enhancing overall configuration manipulability. Our approach employs heuristic designs to define manipulation tasks with key information besides the desired relative poses between the end-effector and targets. We establish a quadratic programming (QP) controller to track these desired poses, enabling the automatic generation of joint trajectories. Additionally, we use Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to optimize placement based on task information, aiming to minimize end-effector pose errors and maximize manipulability. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated through experiments conducted with the BHR humanoid robot.

articleTitle: Paper Shape Tracking System Using Point Cloud and Physical Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: This study introduces a novel paper shape tracking system that utilizes multiple depth cameras and a physical model. The system accomplishes stable paper shape tracking by capturing the paper’s shape as point cloud data from five depth cameras and compensating for any missing data points. We have devised a real-time point cloud registration method to accurately represent the folded state of the paper based on elasto-plastic deformation, enabling precise paper shape tracking. In our experiments, we successfully demonstrated the tracking of the paper’s shape using origami paper.

articleTitle: Investigation of influence factors of embedded droplet printing for generation of cancer cell spheroids with controllable size*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: The cancer cell spheroids, as one of the mostly utilized 3D in vitro model in laboratory, can provide a highly predictive value for the pre-clinical drug research of anticancer therapies. Whereas it is difficult to achieve the precise control over cancer cell spheroids size and composition by conventional methods. Here, we utilized a droplet printing mode of extrusion-based bioprinting to generate cancer cell spheroids in collagen bath. Through altering the settings of droplet printing mode of extrusion-based bioprinting (extrusion time and needle size) and cancer cell concentrations, cancer cell spheroids with different growth profiles and final sizes were generated. Robust bioprinter settings investigation holds the potential to empower researchers with reproducible and reliable platforms for predicting cancer cell spheroids growth profile and final size, and further being applied to evaluate drug efficacy, elucidating molecular mechanisms, and stratifying patient-specific treatment regimens in biomedical fields.

articleTitle: Gait Cycle Detection by Markerless Tracking and Swing Phase Prediction of Paralyzed Leg for Neurostimulation Control*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Nerve stimulation is a technique used to restore walking ability in individuals who have suffered damage to their peripheral nerves. In order to reconstruct the walking motion, it is necessary to coordinate the stimulation with the gait cycle of the healthy parts of the patients. This study employed markerless tracking technology to demonstrate gait cycle identification and estimate the swing phase initiation in the paralyzed leg, utilizing gait periodicity as a basis. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) employing convolutional and pooling layers was applied to identify 22 anatomical landmarks on a rat’s body. The angular positions of the joints and the velocities of the toes were computed based on the body components identified by the CNN. The angles of the joints, velocities of the toes, and time series of both angles and velocities were employed as inputs to categorize the phase of walking. The initiation time of the swing phase in the paralyzed limb was subsequently determined based on the gait phase of the healthy legs. The estimated initiation of the swing phase was compared to the actual initiation of the swing phase in healthy rats. The proposed approach achieved an accuracy of $85 \%$ for detecting the swing phase initiation in the healthy foreleg and approximately $70 \%$ for the hindleg. Nevertheless, the accuracy of estimating the initiation of the swing phase in a paralyzed leg was measured at $60 \%$, indicating a need for improvement. This result came from the difficulty of precisely forecasting non-cyclical leg movements. Identifying non-cyclical moves will improve the estimation accuracy in the future.

articleTitle: A Time-Sequence Decoding Network Based on Frequency Band Power Characteristics for Auditory Attention Decoding*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: The human ability to locate and track a target sound source in a noisy environment, known as the “cocktail party effect”, is a well-studied phenomenon. Auditory attention decoding (AAD) using electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a prominent research focus in this area. Deep learning has significantly advanced AAD performance, yet traditional AAD decoders still leave room for improvement. In this paper, we enhance a widely-used end-to-end ShallowConvNet model (AAD-ShallowConvNet) to improve the detection of auditory spatial attention from EEG signals. ShallowConvNet is traditionally employed to decode EEG band power features. For this study, we optimized the parameters and modules of ShallowConvNet using AAD data. In AAD experiments utilizing a publicly available dataset, AAD-ShallowConvNet demonstrated outstanding performance across different channels and time windows. Under various evaluation conditions, AAD-ShallowConvNet outperformed other state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Cell transfection efficiency improvement via applying stimulation based on the electrically induced microbubbles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: In this research, we achieved the cell transfection via applying electrical and mechanical stimulation to cells. A device called electrically induced microbubble generator was used to generate the electrical and mechanical stimulation. In the previous research, we have achieved the cell transfection through electrically induced microbubbles. To improve the transfection efficiency, we proposed to disrupt the actin cortex layer beneath the cell membrane of suspended cells before cell transfection via microbubble generator. To clarify the influence of the action layer on the transfection, we treated the cells by an actin polymerization inhibitor (cytochalasin D) to influence the actin cortex before applying electromechanical stimulation to the cells. With electrically induced microbubble treatment, the allover actin cortex decreased. With electrically induced microbubble treatment and cytochalasin D before exposure to microbubbles, localized weakness or aggregation of actin was confirmed. We treated the cells with cytochalasin D before applying electromechanical stimulation from microbubble. The results showed that the transfection efficiency of plasmids (4.7/8.3/11 kbp) into NIH/3T3 and UMR-106 cells were improved significantly by this method. Also, the action cortex recovered after incubation. The distribution changing of cortex actin by cytochalasin D treatment before electromechanical exposure is important for causing a partial damage of the cortex actin, that would improve the transfection efficiency or large plasmid transfection.

articleTitle: Multi-Sorting of Large Particles Utilizing Microvortex Generation by High-Speed On-Chip Flow Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Cell sorting is a fundamental technology in single cell analyses. Recently, multi-sorting, which is sorting technique to multi-outlets, has emerged to exploit multi-modal indexes of the cells. However, existing multi-sorting systems are not capable for high-throughput sorting of large ($\sim 100 \mu \mathrm{~m}$) particles. Here, we present an on-chip multi-sorting system of large particles by utilizing microvortex generations. Particularly, the generated vortex develops by engulfing the surrounding fluids and then generate large displacement within 1 ms. Thus, we can rapidly displace large particles to multi-outlets even in the case of a 1 mm wide channels whose wide width hinder to apply previous method to large particle. To demonstrate our system, we verify the regulation of vortex developments and sorting of $100-\mu \mathrm{m}$ beads. As results, we achieved to control the displacement of the vortex and obtain enough displacement to multi-sorting channel within $\mathbf{0. 6 6} \mathbf{~ m s}$. Moreover, we succeeded in sorting of $100-\mu \mathrm{m}$ beads with 4 outlets by regulating the vortex’s displacement. Therefore, our method extends the applicability of on-chip sorting technologies to large particles encompassing cell spheroids, fossil pollen and microalgae/organisms for various research fields.

articleTitle: Visualization of Exercise Intensity During Walking Using Walk-training Robot having Photoplethysmographic Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: This paper reports on a method to visualize exercise intensity, a crucial indicator in gait rehabilitation, using a photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor integrated into a walk-training robot. Improving endurance is known to be effective in preventing and alleviating physical frailty in the elderly, with aerobic exercise being particularly suitable. However, it is challenging for individuals to subjectively determine if they are engaging in aerobic exercise during their workout. To address this, we aim to visualize exercise intensity based on objective indicators by integrating a pulse sensor into the walk-training robot and calculating exercise intensity from the pulse rate during walking. The PPG sensor is integrated inside the handle of the walk-training robot. We calculate exercise intensity using the pulse rate at rest and during walking, along with age, based on the Karvonen formula. We compared the results with a medically certified reference device in stationary, handle-shaking, and walking conditions. In a walking test lasting approximately three minutes, we confirmed that the average pulse rate error compared to the reference device was within 1 bpm. Using this sensor-integrated walk-training robot, we demonstrated the visualization of exercise intensity during walking.

articleTitle: Design and Strength Verification of a Compact VGFL for Sit-to-Stand Assistance Robot*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: This paper introduces a wearable robot which supports frail and elderly people or hemiplegic patients in sit-to-stand transfer of their daily living. The wearable assistive robot is equipped with all components from a power supply to a control system, including variable grounding flexible limbs(VGFL). The VGFL was redesigned to be more compact and stronger than the previous one by optimizing the limb structure so that it could achieve a $40 \%$ reduction in diameter when coiled and a $7 \%$ reduction in limb width, while maintaining a support force of 300 N. In addition to a description of the hardware, this paper also reports on the change in the center of gravity trajectory during standing when using this robot.

articleTitle: Motion Analysis and Design of Bionic Swimming Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Targeting transport is an emerging field in the medical industry that is attempting to obtain a more precise cure for the diseased area. This transport process requires a robot transporter to reach the target. This project aims to develop an E. coli-based swimming robot for precisely delivering medicine to the appointed target area. Key parameters influencing motion are selected through preliminary kinematic analysis in a uniform, viscous fluid. By using the recursion method and differential equation calculation, this project simulated the trajectory related to the robot’s movement and derived the controlling equation. Computer Aided Design (CAD) models are developed under macroscopic dimensions and simulations are performed in liquid environments for validation under microscopic dimensions. A path planning algorithm and a control program with feedback and feedforward control are also developed to stabilize the system. This project has tested the feasibility of different motions under different sets of design specifications and thrust setups, and optimized the related design specifications in the unified viscous flow by Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) analysis. In addition, a control system for the swimmer’s obstacle avoidance and path planning was designed, based on the thrust configurations as inputs. The influence of environment parameters and the robot’s structure is investigated. A robot model capable of moving in a two-dimensional environment is developed correspondingly, which supports further studies’ field tests of micro-robots targeting transport.

articleTitle: Myoelectric Prosthetic Hand with Adjustable Tightening Socket for Varied Residual Limb Shapes*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: The prosthetic socket serves as an interface between the body and the machine. If the socket is not well-fitted to the residual limb, pain can occur. The shape of the residual limb changes over time as surgical scars stabilize or the patient’s body weight fluctuates. A socket with a cutout on the side can be tightened from the outside to adjust its circumference and accommodate these changes. However, when the circumference of the rigid socket is adjusted to fit, soft skin can become trapped due to friction between the skin and the socket. This phenomenon causes pain due to pinching. Consequently, this mechanism cannot be used for myoelectric prosthetic hands, where direct contact between the socket and the skin is necessary. In this study, we developed a socket with a variable circumference that suppresses skin pinching. We applied it to participants with different residual limb shapes. A Box and Block Test (BBT) was performed using two types of sockets. The first used a conventional socket designed to fit their residual limb shape. The second used the proposed socket, which was designed to fit the residual limb’s shape of one out of two participants and adapted to the residual limb’s changing shape. The results of the BBT showed not much difference in the number of blocks moved between the conventional socket and the proposed socket. Therefore, the performance of the proposed socket was comparable to that of conventional sockets and could be applied to different residual limbs. In other words, the proposed socket was shown to adapt to changes in the residual limb without causing pain. Sockets with the proposed functionality could be used in a variety of bio-interfaces, allowing for flexible connections between the body and machines.

articleTitle: Game-based Automated Neurotraining Platform for Bionic Prosthetic Placements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Over the last decade, despite technological advancements in bionic devices, the prosthetic abandonment rate has remained at $50 \%$ or higher. This indicates that the technical capabilities of upper-limb prostheses are not the most relevant aspect in long-term prosthetic adherence. Research has determined that well-structured and patient-tailored prosthetic training on the ability to generate myoelectrical signals is a major determinant in prosthetic adherence over time. As prostheses become more affordable, the volume of prosthetic placements rises, increasing the need for experienced occupational therapists—a need that is unfortunately not being met. Therefore, this system aims to automate the personalization of the neurotraining process through a game interface, enhancing the scalability of the human factor and alleviating the burden of repetitive drills for both the patient and the facilitator. This work presents a novel approach that combines personalized gamification and myoelectric proficiency quantification to revolutionize rehabilitation practices within the bionic industry.

articleTitle: Design and 3D Printing of Lower Limb Prosthetic Socket *
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: The prosthetic socket is a crucial interface connecting the residual limb to the prosthetic device, significantly affecting force transmission and wearer comfort. This work presents a comprehensive framework for design, simulation, and fabrication of the prosthetic socket. A 3D model of the residual limb, including the skeleton model and skin contour, is reconstructed from CT scan data. Using this model, the prosthetic socket and liner are designed based on biomechanical principles. The interaction force between the residual limb and the prosthetic socket and liner is simulated via finite element analysis (FEA) when the body weight of a below-knee amputee exerts on the prosthetic socket. Finally, the prosthetic socket and residual limb are fabricated using additive manufacturing (AM) technology, and a soft prosthetic liner is made of ethylene-vinyl-acetate (EVA) polymer. Clinical trials on a below-knee amputee were conducted to preliminarily test the prosthetic socket’s performance.

articleTitle: Mechanism design and performance analysis of a novel truss-shaped deployable manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: To grasp various non-cooperative objects in space, this paper develops a novel truss-shaped deployable manipulator with double scissor-shaped mechanisms, which consists of multi-fingers and a single-mobility base mechanism. To enhance its scalability, the modular design idea is used in the design of the finger, the workspace of the deployable manipulator can thus be adjusted by the number of finger modules according to actual requirement. Besides, the double scissor-shaped mechanisms offer a good deploy/fold ratio for the deployable manipulator, which provides convenience for transportation and storage. More importantly, a good deploy/fold ratio ensures a large workspace for grasping tasks. In addition, unique design of the single-mobility base mechanism further optimizes deploy/fold performance, the driver design can also be simplified while the initial grasping angle can be effectively formed. In the specific content, design of the deployable manipulator is first detailed illustrated. Then, the performance analysis is performed to obtain the kinematic index. In addition, grasping analysis and simulation is carried out, which effectively validates grasping performance, the result shows that the deployable manipulator has a good grasping adaptability, and many objects with different sizes and shapes can be effectively grasped.

articleTitle: Development of a Microrobot Screening System Driven by Combined Magnetic Fields and Optoelectronic Tweezers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Drug-loaded microrobots can be utilized for targeted drug delivery. However, the probability of drug loading onto microrobots ranges only between 50% and 90%. To enhance the drug-carrying capacity of the final microrobots, we developed a microrobot screening system (MRSS). MRSS employs a hybrid driving method by combining electromagnetic drive and optoelectronic tweezers (OET) drive, along with the introduction of visual image recognition, to achieve the goal of excluding non-drug-carrying microrobots. MRSS allows for efficient removal of microrobots not carrying drugs from the swarm, with the potential to exclude multiple targets simultaneously. MRSS has broad application prospects in cell screening, assembly, and monitoring.

articleTitle: Decomposition of 3D Joint Angle by Kinematic Modeling of Free Flight Pigeon Forelimb
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Birds utilize complex coupled motions in their forelimbs to maintain exceptional flight performance. Understanding these dynamics is essential for designing biomimetic unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Typically, the forelimb skeleton of birds is modeled as a spatial six-bar linkage mechanism through the analysis of physical specimens. However, the detailed description of skeletal transformations in birds during free flight remains uncharted. To address this gap, we propose an open-chain kinematic model to simulate the skeletal motion variations of pigeons (Columba livia) in free flight. Kinematic data of pigeon wings were collected during free flight, and the skeletal model was fitted to the collected data using global optimization. This allowed us to derive the joint motion angles of the skeleton during the take-off, leveling flight, and landing phases. This study elucidates the mechanisms of bird wing deformation, providing valuable insights and guidance for developing bio-inspired flying robots.

articleTitle: Microfluidic Formation of Porous Microgels with Interior Spiral Canals for Mesenchymal Stem Cell Culture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Stem cell delivery is pivotal in tissue engineering, enabling the regeneration and repair of damaged tissues and advancing therapeutic solutions. As an innovative stem cell delivery system, microgels provide a supportive, protective environment that enhances cell viability and promotes targeted tissue regeneration. However, conventional microgels face limitations due to the lack of microporous structures and interior canals, which hinder efficient nutrient and oxygen exchange, thereby reducing cell viability and proliferation. To overcome these challenges, we developed a droplet microfluidic system for the stable and continuous production of porous microgels with interior spiral canals by introducing a pore-forming agent. This controlled formation process results in microgels with excellent porosity and monodispersity. With their unique structure and biocompatibility, these porous microgels are excellent microcarriers for 3D cell culture, enhancing nutrient and oxygen exchange and providing a conducive environment for cell growth and proliferation.

articleTitle: Underwater Glider Actuated by Bioinspired Soft Swim Bladder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Underwater gliders are recognized as highly efficient tools for marine exploration due to their low power consumption. The buoyancy driven system plays a critical role in the design of underwater gliders. Traditionally, hydraulic systems using motors, pumps, and valves were commonly employed in underwater glider designs, resulting in high energy consumption and noise levels. This research introduces an innovative approach by utilizing a bioinspired soft swim bladder (BSSB) to actuate the underwater glider. The BSSB offers advantages such as reduced power consumption and noise, making it particularly suitable for sensitive underwater environments. The BSSB is developed based on an electro-pneumatic dielectric elastomer actuator with a spherical crown shape. Experimental investigations were conducted to analyze the relationship between volume change and loading path. The volume change achieved was up to 4.2 mL, representing a 300% increase due to the adjustment of the loading path. Subsequently, an untethered, self-powered underwater glider prototype was developed and tested to verify its underwater gliding capabilities. This study highlights the potential of utilizing a BSSB for propelling underwater gliders. Future research will focus on the control mechanisms for the underwater glider actuated by the BSSB and strategies to enhance its operational performance.

articleTitle: Learning to Turn: Deformation Control of a Novel Flexible Fishtail Actuated by Artificial Muscles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Achieving agile, fish-like turning remains a critical challenge in the development of robotic fish. The flexible deformation of a fish’s body significantly contributes to its turning ability. Consequently, researchers have devoted substantial efforts to enhancing the compliance and agility of robotic fish. This paper presents a novel flexible fishtail, inspired by the musculoskeletal structure of real fish, which can control the deformation of its flexible components during turns, improving the turning performance of robotic fish. The fishtail primarily consists of a carbon fiber plate with attached artificial muscles. These muscles can contract and stretch, causing the carbon fiber tail to bend and deform. To enable precise deformation control, a dynamic model of the fishtail is established based on Hamilton’s principle. Subsequently, deep reinforcement learning methods such as deep deterministic policy gradient and soft actor-critic are employed to develop a deformation controller under joint deflection. Cross-validation ensures the controller’s accuracy and robustness. The experimental results demonstrate that this controller facilitates the deformation control of the flexible tail across various turning amplitudes and speeds, allowing the fishtail to exhibit adjustable compliance or resistance to fluids during turning motion. Consequently, this enhances the agility of the robotic fish.

articleTitle: Segmentation of continuous stimulus response patterns in a cultured neuronal network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: In this study, we developed a cultured neuronal circuit as a simplified model of the brain. Our objective was to investigate the emergence of language acquisition elements within this minimal living model, particularly focusing on the segmentation of input series stimulation. Our hypothesis posited that within this cultured neuronal circuit, the segmentation of series stimuli would manifest through an emphasized response pattern to a specific repeated sequence of input patterns. Initially, we observed a notable augmentation in the reproducibility of response patterns following repeated series stimulation from a single electrode. Specifically, the reproducibility of responses to continuous stimulation intervals of 1 s appeared to significantly increase. Moreover, we confirmed a link between the increased reproducibility of response patterns to series stimulation and the stability of background activity. Additionally, we analyzed the mutual similarity of invoked response to triple stimuli (triplets) from three independent electrodes, $\mathbf{A}, \mathrm{B}$, and $\mathbf{C}$, in various permutations (e.g., ABC, BCA, etc.). By applying 10 series-stimuli with equalized triplet occurrence frequencies, the reproducibility of response patterns invoked by each triplet stimulus was standardized, suggesting that when triplet stimuli are input with equal frequencies, their responses exhibit comparable reproducibility. If the input frequencies of triplet stimuli are biased, and if the reproducibility of responses to specific triplet stimuli with higher input frequencies increases, it implies the segmentation of these triplet stimulus patterns as cohesive units akin to words. In future analyses, we will investigate the reproducibility of responses to sequences with biased triplet occurrence frequencies.

articleTitle: MMG-based real-time wrist tremor detection for exoskeleton integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is often characterised by distal tremor, affecting the patient’s hands and preventing them from performing daily tasks. There has been an increase in tremor suppression orthoses in the last decade, specifically containing active components that employ bio-signals for closed-loop control. However, most sensors tend to focus on the motion output for tremor detection, which is prone to inaccuracies and can hinder the responsiveness of the system. With the integration of machine learning in real-time tremor detection, this would enable the analysis of more complex signals, such as the muscle activation patterns of the subject’s forearm, which would give us indications on tremorgenic states based on the contractions rather than the resulting kinematics.This study therefore investigates the use of mechanomyography (MMG) as a sensing modality for muscle activity, and its capacity to detect tremor in a real-time setting for applications in tremor suppression devices. Wrist tremor is induced through transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation, which enables the assessment of this approach as a proxy to PD tremor, and the ability of the MMG to work in conjunction with stimulation.Results show that the MMG-based algorithm was capable of effectively detecting when visible tremor was present, based purely on the muscle contraction patterns. This paves the way towards the use of MMG in closed-loop control systems of tremor suppression devices.

articleTitle: Consistency-based Gait Generation for Terrain-blind Bipedal Walking via V-SLIP Model and Reinforcement Learning*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Terrain-blind walking ability is significant for biped robots to address unforeseen obstacles and terrain modeling errors. To achieve the stable and robustness walking on unknown terrain, this paper proposed a consistency-based gait generation method for terrain-blind bipedal walking via the V-SLIP model and Reinforcement learning method. Firstly, a real-time gait generation scheme based on the Variable Spring-Loaded Pendulum (V-SLIP) model is proposed, which considers a consistency-based gait generation strategy. Secondly, a reinforcement learning-driven controller is designed to regulate the motion trajectory, which is realized by adjusting leg stiffness values to compensate for unexpected terrain height changes. Finally, the proposed method is verified through simulation experiments. Experimental results indicate that the stable terrain-blind walking via V-SLIP model with a random terrain height change of 0.05 m and a walking speed of $1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ is realized.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Human-Centric Shoulder Exoskeleton to Improve the Range of Motion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: The upper limb exoskeletons available in the market are used to assist in carrying out activities of daily living (ADL) but have a limited range of motion (ROM). The limitation in ROM is due to the negligence of the complete shoulder complex joint motions while designing the wearable exoskeleton. This can affect the shoulder joint components due to interaction forces generated between the exoskeleton and the human shoulder in the presence of joint misalignment. This paper proposes a novel design of a human-centric shoulder exoskeleton mechanism. It is capable of exhibiting the same reachability of the human shoulder without a self-collision or collision with the human body throughout the ROM by introducing kinematic redundancy. The design procedure of the exoskeleton, which considers human joint motions, has been presented along with the static stress analysis. The actuator selection for the glenohumeral joint has also been specified along with the initial 3D printed prototype of the exoskeleton mechanism, which is further used to test and compare its maximum ROM.

articleTitle: Wavy Whiskers in Phocid Seals Exhibit High Signal-to-Noise in Sensing Hydrodynamic Flows
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Phocid seals can detect fish from distances up to 180 meters solely using undulating whiskers. The unique undulating surfaces of these whiskers have been found to minimize vortex-induced vibrations (VIVs). In our previous work, we measured the ratios of undulation wavelength (λ) to mean diameter $\left(D_{m}\right),\left(\lambda / D_{m}\right)$ in both harbor and grey seals, yielding values of approximately 4.36 and 4.63, respectively. In this study, we delve into the significance of the $\lambda / D_{m}$ ratio to the vibration responses of seal whiskers in a fluid flow. We conducted comprehensive fluid-structure interaction studies using COMSOL Multiphysics®, wherein we studied vibration responses of harbor and grey seal whisker structures with diverse $\lambda / D_{m}$ values in the oncoming flow. Our results indicate that seal whiskers exhibited a trough in their VIV responses and a peak in wake-induced vibration (WIV) responses at $\lambda / D_{m}$ values around 4 to 5. Our findings could imply that the evolutionary optimization of the $\lambda / D_{m}$ value enables seal whiskers with resistance to VIV and sensitivity to WIV.

articleTitle: Vision Servoing Endovascular Interventional Robot System: Design and Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: In vascular interventions, visual feedback based on DSA images is essential for making interventional action decisions. Real-time DSA images provide crucial feedback on the position of the guidewire tip within the vasculature. When excessive bending of the guidewire tip is detected, interventional radiologists manipulate the guidewire by retracting or rotating it to prevent damage to the intimal surface. This paper aims to integrate visual feedback into the closed-loop control of vascular robots, creating a safe and intelligent vascular interventional robot system. We propose a distributed hardware and software architecture for the vascular interventional robot, building on our previous designs. This architecture allows the robot to support and control various combinations of instruments, ensuring effective data and command transmission between modules. Based on this foundation, we introduce a vision servoing robot control strategy. The microwire target in the DSA image is segmented, and the bending energy is calculated based on the wire’s curve. This energy is then nonlinearly constrained to form a closed-loop control logic. We deployed the vascular interventional robot system in a standard interventional operating room and conducted experiments on vascular phantoms. These experiments verified the robot’s teleoperation functionality, communication latency between modules, and the enhancement of procedural safety and intelligence through vision servoing. The quantitative evaluation indicated that the vision servoing function significantly mitigates the bending of the microwire tip, enabling a smoother completion of the interventional task.

articleTitle: On-Chip Automated Acoustofluidic Three-Dimensional Observation System for Oocytes*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cyborg and Bionic Systems (CBS)
abstract: Single-cell manipulation techniques are an important topic in medical and biological research, especially in assisted reproductive technology. The traditional method of observing oocytes through contact manipulation using a capillary is inefficient, requires a high level of skill, and poses potential damage to the oocytes. Therefore, we propose an on-chip acoustofluidic system for the automated observation of oocytes. Multiple trap chambers allow for the simultaneous capture of multiple cells, increasing operational efficiency. Fluid-based trapping and acoustofluidic-driven rotation reduce the probability of oocytes encountering sharp ends, making them less susceptible to damage. Our system has been tested and proven capable of rotating the oocyte in both in-plane and out-of-plane directions, which enables the adjustment of the oocyte to an arbitrary orientation in space. The whole process does not involve the movement of the focal plane. By combining the proposed automated oocyte position recognition method with the pulse width modulation-based position control method, we achieved a maximum speed of 1.4 revolutions per second and a minimum control accuracy of less than 1.6°, making it user-friendly with almost no operational threshold.
